title: The Indexes Are Hiding How Weak This Market Really Is

 Most stocks are already in a bear market, and that may turn out to be good news for stock pickers.

 The Invesco QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) is down about 0.3% early Tuesday as Monday’s selling momentum continues. Asian markets were weak overnight after new U.S. licensing rules for chips going to data centers in Southeast Asia added to the pressure on technology stocks.
 Nvidia’s ( NVDA ) earnings tonight are the main event, and they could bring us closer to a tradable low. Investors are clearly nervous, and with Jensen Huang gone, it is unclear what they now expect. 
 Wall Street is forecasting revenue of about $109 billion, but Nvidia stock will move on what interim CEO Colette Kress says about next year and about how the company finances its customers. Options are pricing in a move of roughly 9% in either direction, which is the biggest move they have priced in for an Nvidia report since 2024.
 IBD Is Jerked Around Again
 After Monday’s selling, Investor’s Business Daily lowered its recommended exposure back to 0% to 20%, just three trading days after last Wednesday’s follow-through day prompted it to raise exposure. By my count, it has changed its exposure level six times in less than four weeks.
 IBD says the rally attempt is technically still intact because the Nasdaq is holding above its intraday low of Nov. 5, but the index has undercut the low of the first day of the rally attempt, and IBD says the rally is “on the ropes.”
 The Indexes Aren’t the Market
 IBD’s problems illustrate how ineffective it is to time the market using the indexes when most stocks are already in a bear market. In a more normal market, there is a correlation between the movement of the indexes and the majority of stocks, but this hasn’t been the case for a long time because of the narrow AI strength that persisted. More than 62% of stocks are below their 200-day moving averages, while the S&P 500 is still above its own.
 Trying to navigate this market by looking at the indexes is a mistake, but it persists because the indexes are convenient for media reporting and create an illusion of precision. If you want to know what is going on in the market, it is necessary to focus on individual stock charts and on which sectors are showing strength. That takes more effort, but it will give you much better insight.
 The good news is that a market that is punishing individual stocks to a greater degree than the indexes should benefit stock pickers when conditions improve, and there is a good chance that could occur in conjunction with strong end-of-the-year seasonality.
 Game Plan
 My game plan for a while has been to maintain high levels of cash and stay patient while waiting for individual charts to develop. The current market stress is occurring at the right time for a turn, just as positive seasonality starts to build into the end of the year. 
 I’m not expecting a wild end-of-the-year rally, but so many stocks have been punished due to market conditions rather than fundamentals that there will be some great trades when the pressure is finally lifted.
 As I discussed Monday, I have been making some incremental buys of Amazon ( AMZN ), as I believe it is a stock that will be a leader in cloud computing and will bounce back quickly once the general AI pressure starts to relent.
 There are also many small-caps that are innocent victims of market conditions, but it is important to wait for technical improvement before putting any significant money into them. Too many investors are trapped in downtrends because they think valuation will provide support, but in a market like this, that doesn’t work well.
 At the time of publication, Rev Shark was long NVD and AMZN .
 By James "Rev Shark" DePorre
